summary: Keep authenticated notice sources and person controls independent of the disposable runtime snapshot, with a stable source-derived NoticeId.

replay.detail: Source and control authority no longer reads or compares the runtime. Only snapshots require the current designated runtime. Quiet custom caches rebuild at projection version 3 to enforce the new reviewed pins. Existing signed claims are not rewritten. Generic custom data written under the reserved notice prefixes before notice reservation, including by released v0.3.x generic writers, is not notice history and stays hidden. Facts from untagged interim builds before this change are not migrated.

schema.detail: Re-pin the unreleased v1 source and control manifests in place, removing runtime fields; no v2 prefix or compatibility alias is introduced. NoticeId is notice/ followed by the immutable source UUID, not a disposable snapshot subject. Native Rust, TypeScript, Effect and Swift models derive from the shared schema.

rules.detail: Producer source authorship, immutable source links and the person recipient's control authority remain authenticated independently of payloads. A trusted member asserting the designated runtime or recipient actor is not detected. It is the same fleet-member trust as the existing relay, and end-to-end actor authentication is out of scope.

compatibility.detail: Internal notice models still advertise no native operation or capability. Generic reserved reads remain unavailable. Older intermediate notice pins are not accepted as the current contract.

downtime.detail: No deployment outage is required for the tagged-release fleet.

manual.detail: No supported notice-history migration is required; the native notice writer has not shipped in a tagged release.

recovery.detail: Handover uses discarded and rebuilt snapshots, not portable historical admission certificates. A partition that has not observed revocation may continue accepting old-runtime snapshots. Action revocation takes effect at the persisted owner's acknowledgement fence, not remote graph publication; a stale owner retains residual exposure. Owner binding, acknowledgement and action routing are not implemented by this lineage slice.
